learning_outcomes.text: Understand the basic logic and functioning mechanisms of the market economy; become familiar with microeconomic fundamentals (costs, productivity, demand, supply, prices, profit, etc.); be exposed to highly topical subjects such as the role of uncertainty and information; analyze the break-even point; understand how consumers make decisions; understand how producers make decisions in different types of markets; comprehend the fundamentals of economic policy decisions.

Develop the necessary skills for calculating costs, productivity, prices, profit, break-even point, etc.; Understand how a firm decides whether to increase or decrease the quantity produced or prices, if it is at the optimal point or if, on the contrary, it must restrict its activity.

syllabus_topics: System of economic-social activities: Needs and economic resources
System of economic-social activities: The economic system and its structure
Contemporary market economy: Types of economic systems
Contemporary market economy: Market economy: definition, characteristics
Economic agents: Concept, typology of economic agents
Economic agents: Commercial companies
Factors of production: System of factors of production
Factors of production: Labor, nature, capital, neofactors of production
Utilization of factors of production: Combination of factors of production
Utilization of factors of production: Production cost. Content, Cost function
Productivity of factors of production: Forms of productivity
Productivity of factors of production: Productivity of labor, capital, natural factor
Economic goods. Their utility and value: Economic goods. Utility of goods
Economic goods. Their utility and value: Economic value
Prices and market mechanism: Content and functions of price
Prices and market mechanism: Price formation in the market economy
Market, competition, demand and supply: Market and competition
Market, competition, demand and supply: Demand and supply
Money and monetary circulation: Money. Money supply and liquidity
Money and monetary circulation: Value or purchasing power of money
Theory of income. Wages, principal form of income: Labor market
Theory of income. Wages, principal form of income: Wages. Determination of wage size in the market economy
Profit. Interest. Rent: Notion of profit; Profit indicators
Profit. Interest. Rent: Monetary market and credit; Interest. Concept, indicators and forms
Profit. Interest. Rent: Rent in neoclassical theory and new forms of rent
Economic indicators; Theory of production factors. Defining the subject of economic theory study. Types of reasoning used by economists and some techniques
Production cost. Evolution of short-term costs. Long-term production costs. Economies of scale
Productivity of factors. Labor productivity, capital factor productivity and natural factor productivity
Utility. Analysis of how the quantities of goods and services consumers will demand at different price and income levels are determined
Market and competition. Price in the market economy. Demand and supply. Price. Perfect competition and imperfect competition
Wages. Marginal product revenue of the labor factor. Marginal product value. Labor supply. Determination of equilibrium wage. Imperfections in the labor market. Influence of trade unions
Profit, interest and rent. Calculation of total and unit profit, profit rates, simple and compound interest

assessment_methods.method: Written exam (covering knowledge and application capacity)
Applied activities (seminar grade and attendance, two written assignments)

assessment_rules: The final grade (Nf) is calculated as 0.66 times the written exam average (Ne) plus 0.33 times the applied activities grade (Np). The written exam average (Ne) is the arithmetic mean of two written assignments (Np1, Np2), covering chapters I-VI and VII-XII respectively. Students must pass two written assignments during the seminar activities. A minimum of 50% of the total score is required to pass the discipline.
